subject.title: [security] XCP-ng HOST_IS_SLAVE redirect can re-send pool password to a response-selected host

question: Which XCP-ng pool-master destinations may receive password-bearing retries: only the configured origin, explicitly configured additional origins, or origins proven through another authenticated pool-membership mechanism?
rationale: The replay is unsafe, but the source and tests do not define which cross-origin pool layouts are legitimate, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent credential-destination contract.

options.title: Explicit master allowlist
options.body: Trust the configured origin by default and permit additional pool-master origins only when the operator explicitly approves them.

options.title: Exact same origin
options.body: Reject every scheme, hostname, or effective-port change, maximizing safety but potentially breaking existing multi-host pools.

options.title: Authenticated pool membership
options.body: Allow a changed origin only after an independently authenticated mechanism proves that it belongs to the configured XCP-ng pool.

recommendation.title: Explicit master allowlist
recommendation.body: Trust the configured origin by default and permit additional pool-master origins only when the operator explicitly approves them.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged history shows the strongest XCP-ng domain context for the intended redirect behavior and supported pool layouts.
